name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 14
aliases: Combined Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency Type 14

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Early onset multisystemic symptoms including neurological and muscular involvement
Deficient activity of multiple respiratory chain complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Pathogenic variants identified in nuclear genes affecting oxidative phosphorylation
Brain MRI showing Leigh-like lesions or basal ganglia abnormalities
Elevated lactate levels in blood or cerebrospinal fluid

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus biochemical evidence and genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

searchTerms: developmental delay with loss of skills

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate
Multiple respiratory chain enzyme deficiencies in muscle biopsy
imaging: MRI brain with bilateral symmetric basal ganglia and brainstem lesions
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy showing lactate peak
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation proteins
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and mitochondrial proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly neurological presentation with characteristic MRI lesions
Usually caused by mutations in mitochondrial or nuclear genes distinct from COXPD14
Stroke-like episodes and mitochondrial DNA mutations
More prominent stroke-like episodes and hearing loss

redFlags: Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Multisystem involvement including cardiomyopathy and liver dysfunction
references: Rahman S, et al. Mitochondrial disease: clinical features and diagnosis. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2017;40(4):569-580.
Parikh S, et al. Diagnosis and management of mitochondrial disease: a consensus statement from the Mitochondrial Medicine Society. Genet Med. 2015;17(9):689-701.
